question:
(i) State Gauss’s law for magnetism.
(ii) Explain why the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
(iii) What does this imply about the existence of isolated magnetic poles?

options.A:
(i) Gauss’s law for magnetism is $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec S=\mu_0I$.
(ii) Net flux is zero only when there is no current inside the surface.
(iii) Therefore, isolated north and south poles can exist.
options.B:
(i) Gauss’s law for magnetism is $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec S=\mu_0q_m$.
(ii) Magnetic lines begin and end on isolated poles.
(iii) Hence, a magnet can have only one pole.
options.C:
(i) Gauss’s law for magnetism states $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec S=0$.
(ii) Magnetic field lines form continuous closed curves, so equal flux enters and leaves every closed surface and the net flux is zero.
(iii) An isolated magnetic pole would give non-zero net flux, so isolated poles do not exist.
options.D:
(i) $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec S=B(2\pi r)$.
(ii) The flux is zero because magnetic fields have no direction.
(iii) Thus, every magnet has only a north pole.
